issues.situation: The fix blocks every unit from going home, but the evidence only supports redirecting one of them. The situation: round 1, player 1, own home empty after the AI deployed its own army, a card that never pays for home (8 of 25 pairings: Immovable Object, Purge and Secure, Unstoppable Force, Meatgrinder, Reconnaissance Sweep, Delaying Action, Outmanoeuvre, Smoke and Mirrors), and the enemy out of reach. In this situation the base usually plans two units for home (the cluster title; s7468 Gamma + Alpha; s7411 Gamma + Beta). r1_home_later rejects every move or advance to that home. In the designer's own s7468 replay it logged three skips (Gamma, Beta, Alpha), nobody went home, Alpha and Beta stacked on obj_nml_1, and Beta dropped its centre race. That plan was never measured. Every positive measurement redirected one unit while another still went home. At s7468 the forced alternative B (+6.86) still sent Alpha home. At s7411 r1 P1 movement_2 (Purge and Secure, +2.50 [0.71, 4.29], n36) Gamma was redirected after Beta already stood on home. The only measurement that redirected the other home unit is s7411 r1 P1 movement_1: Beta to Move obj_nml_1 while Gamma was still planned for home gave -3.08 [-6.27, +0.10] (n12), on a card this fix fires on. Leaving home empty has later costs that a one-round replay of B does not show. WEIGHT_HOME_UNDEFENDED is not limited to round 1, so in round 2 the empty home scores about 21 (10 uncontrolled + 9 undefended + 2 round-2 urgency) against about 14-18 for an empty NML objective under these cards. The round-2 plan therefore sends a unit back, now from about 17" (2 moves at s7468), so the capture is delayed, not saved. Home is also empty when enemy reserves can arrive: _keeper_release_threat's own model lets them arrive from round 2, and 6 Ork units were in reserve at s7468. And home cannot score Defend Stronghold if that card is drawn in round 2.
issues.proposed_change: Skip at most ONE unit per home objective per movement phase. The first (top-scored) home capturer goes to its next objective. Every later home candidate is allowed: pass 2, the COORD-4 backfill and the pass-3 support. Store the skipped unit id in a static keyed by player + battle round + objective (like _turn_movement_plan), so a replan keeps skipping that same unit and lets the next one through. At s7468 this gives exactly the measured B (Gamma Advance obj_center, Alpha to home). Add a 2-unit test (one unit goes forward, one goes home). Before shipping, replay s7468 and s7411 movement_1 with the revised code and measure the plan it actually produces, not B.

issues.situation: It cannot fire in any benchmark fixture, so the bench will give identical pairs and cannot show a gain (as V9's keeper fix did, 124/124). In all three fixtures, both home objectives start held by deployed units, so the home state is held_safe and never 'uncontrolled' (details in fires_in_bench). The single keepers hold all of round 1 (FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE is off in V9R), and the fix is off from round 2. The design report does not estimate bench firing at all.
issues.proposed_change: No change within this cluster can make it fire there, because the keeper is deployed on the objective. Do not spend bench arms on it. If it is merged, treat it as a param-gated no-op for the bench and decide on rollout evidence only (the revised one-unit rule, measured at s7468 and s7411).

issues.situation: Units can still reach home through pass 3. A unit skipped by r1_home_later is not added to extra_obj_skipped, so its pass-3 support_allowed list is empty, and _find_best_remaining_objective can still pick the uncontrolled home (priority still includes +9) as a 'support' Move. The pass-2 capture is blocked, but a pass-3 support move to the same home is allowed. The cluster's 'reinforcing obj_home_1 (1 unit already committed)' pattern (s7405, s7411 movement_1) comes from this support pass, which the fix does not touch. A slow unit whose only reachable objective is home just changes from a capture to a support move.
issues.proposed_change: Apply the same rule in pass 3: count r1-skipped units in extra_obj_skipped, or exclude the skipped home from that unit's support_allowed. With the one-unit rule, let the allowed home unit come from either pass, so exactly one unit ends up assigned to home.

issues.situation: The 'pays nothing' test reads only the primary card and ignores plan orders. KEEPER-RELEASE keeps a unit whose candidate carries a PM-3 HOLD_OBJECTIVE earmark; this fix does not check c.earmark. The shipped Ork plans (orks_free_grab_grip / orks_recon_stomps) earmark Gretchin with HOLD_OBJECTIVE obj_home_1, so a plan order to take home would be overridden in round 1. Their crucible deployment already puts models on home, so the risk is small there. Secondary cards that pay for home are also ignored: Defend Stronghold from round 2, and Burden of Trust, whose auto-assigned home guard is the nearest unit (Gamma at s7468). Note that the measured B already gave up Burden of Trust's round-1 home score.
issues.proposed_change: In r1_home_later, return false when str(c.get('earmark','')).begins_with('HOLD_OBJECTIVE'). Treat a 'home' hint in _get_secondary_awareness(player).vp_objective_hints as paying for home. With the one-unit rule a home unit still remains, so this mainly protects authored plans.

reviews.strengths: Very conservative trigger. It acts only in round 1, only on our own uncontrolled home, and only when the card counts home in none of the rules active now or scoring at the next Command phase; an unknown card or legacy scoring never fires. The threat envelope over-estimates reach, and for the second player any enemy reserve blocks it, so in practice it is player-1 only. Keepers and rounds 2-5 are untouched, so it agrees with all three harmful guardrails (s7404 r1 P1, s7468 r1 P2 Kommandos, s7451 r1 P2). The decoy exception is correct: MissionManager's smoke_and_mirrors action skips _is_home_objective_11e, so a home objective is never decoyed. Param 0 restores the base exactly, and the new argument defaults to false, so KEEPER-RELEASE is unchanged. It reuses helpers that V9R keeps with the same signatures and does not need FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE on. At s7468 it produces the measured unit, objective and mode for Gamma (Advance obj_center). Its direction is supported on a second eligible card: s7411 Purge and Secure measured +2.50 for sending the second home unit forward. It adds no bench risk. The report is candid: its risks (1), (2) and (5) anticipate the issues above.
reviews.summary: Narrow and safe, but it does nothing in the benchmark. In all three fixtures both homes start held by deployed units (Custodian Guard F on area-large-14/13; 4-5 Ork units on each Ork home), so it fires 0 times in either seat and every bench pair will be identical: the bench cannot show a gain. Where it does fire (games where the AI deployed its own army, player 1, round 1, empty home, 8 of 25 cards), it blocks every unit from home. The measured gains instead redirected one unit while another still went home (s7468 B: Alpha; s7411 movement_2: Beta). The only measured redirect of that other home unit was negative (s7411 movement_1: -3.08 [-6.27, +0.10], Purge and Secure). The empty home is then valued at about 21 again in round 2 (WEIGHT_HOME_UNDEFENDED applies in every round), so a forward unit walks about 2 moves back, and home is open when the engine's threat model lets reserves arrive. The fix's actual plan at s7468 (nobody home, Alpha and Beta stacked on obj_nml_1, Beta off the centre) was never measured. Of the cluster's findings on V9, only s7468 changes; its gain comes mostly from Smoke and Mirrors' decoy income, which keeps paying every turn, and the s7451 finding (Normal vs Advance) is untouched. Revise: skip at most one unit per home per phase (kept across replans), close the pass-3 support leak, and keep units under a HOLD_OBJECTIVE earmark. Then measure the revised plan at s7468 and s7411 movement_1. Even revised it will not fire in the bench, so it can only be judged on rollout evidence. Files reviewed: /home/user/warhammer-40k-godot/tools/ai_lab/r4_designs/r1_home_capture/narrow.patch and narrow.json.

issues.situation:
The fix's own plan was never value-checked.
- s7468 r1 P1: the skip also stops Alpha and Beta going home. All three go forward, and Beta gives up its centre race. The measured +6.86 alternative B still sent Alpha home, and the critic asked for one unit on a safe home. The designer's 2-seed run was base vs B, not fix vs base.
- s7403 r1 P2 (measured_positions: clear, +8.67, n=36) is unchecked, but every trigger condition holds there (checked from the save). P2's card Unstoppable Force never counts home. P2's home is empty. P2 has the first turn, so enemy_round = 1. The six Ork reserves have no enhancement and no early-arrival rule. The nearest on-board Ork is 29.1" from the home area against a 24" reach. The base plan sent a unit to obj_home_2 (critic note), and the clearly better alternative also put a unit (the nearer Prosecutors) on home. With the fix, no unit goes home.
issues.proposed_change: Before selection, run rollout.py on the fix's full plan vs base (>= 12 seeds) at s7468 r1 P1 and s7403 r1 P2. If either loses, narrow the skip so that one unit can still take home: skip a unit's home capture only while another unassigned unit that reaches home this turn remains, choosing the cheaper unit or the one with the lower best-elsewhere score (KEEPER-PICK style). This reproduces branch B at s7468.

issues.situation: False decision text. A redirected unit gets no coordination_note and no extra_obj_skipped entry. OBJ-EXPLAIN-1 then takes its top candidate (home, 38.1 at s7468), finds no takers, and writes 'obj_home_1 already has enough OC — sent to obj_center instead'. That note becomes the decision record's override_reason (around line 4032). Home actually has 0 OC. The LLM critic sweeps read these records.
issues.proposed_change: In pass 2, record r1_home_skipped[uid] = oid. Before OBJ-EXPLAIN-1, set assignments[uid].coordination_note = 'not capturing <home> in round 1 — our primary does not pay for it and no enemy can reach it before our next turn; sent to <oid> instead' when the unit went elsewhere. Do not reuse extra_obj_skipped, because that would also restrict pass-3 support.

issues.situation: The trigger reads only the primary card, but the const and log say home 'pays nothing yet'. Burden of Trust is in the 11e deck and scores from round 1 at the end of the opponent's turn (2 VP per guarded objective). At s7468 it was active, and Gamma was obj_home_1's designated guard (guards map in the save). The s7468 measurement already includes losing that guard and was still +6.86, so this does not block.
issues.proposed_change: Either reword the const, comment and log to say 'our primary does not pay for it' and name Burden of Trust as a known cost, or add a check that _get_secondary_awareness(player).defend_home == 0. The second option would also stop the fix firing at s7468.

issues.situation: Pass 3 can undo the skip. A skipped unit with no other objective needing OC falls to _find_best_remaining_objective. Its support_allowed set is empty and the function ignores the skip. Home has the +9 undefended priority and is nearest, so the unit can still walk home as 'supporting nearby objective'. overcommit_redirect also does not call r1_home_later; this path is dead while FIX_OVERCOMMIT = 0.
issues.proposed_change: When other objectives exist, pass an allowed_ids set without the skipped home for that unit, or document that pass 3 may still go home. Add `or r1_home_later.call(alt)` to overcommit_redirect's filters for when FIX_OVERCOMMIT is turned on.

reviews.fires_in_bench:
Expected 0 fires in all 3 fixtures, for both seats and every seed, so all pairs should play out identically (like V9's keeper fix, 124/124).

- The trigger needs our home to be 'uncontrolled' when a round-1 Movement plan is built.
- All six homes start held: Custodian Guard F on each side in the Custodes mirror; Guard F (P1) and 5 Ork units (P2) in the asym fixture; 4 Ork units on each home in the Orks mirror.
- No unit on a home has 10+ models (no AGGRO-FREE), FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE is OFF on V9R, and no fixture has reserves.
- The plan is built once per phase while home is held_safe, so the keeper holds.
- The trigger is gated to round 1, so it never fires in later rounds.
- The card condition alone would pass for 8 of 25 pairings, about 32% per seat: Immovable Object, Purge and Secure, Unstoppable Force, Meatgrinder, Reconnaissance Sweep, Delaying Action, Outmanoeuvre, Smoke and Mirrors. The home-state check fails first in every fixture.
reviews.strengths:
- Small and gated by FIX_R1_HOME_CAPTURE. At 0 the closure returns false immediately and the new skip_home_decoy flag defaults to false for KEEPER-RELEASE, so behaviour is exactly the base; the only side effect is one extra param read per call.
- Reuses round-3's checked KEEPER-RELEASE helpers for the primary card and the threat.
- The decoy reasoning is correct: MissionManager never decoys a home objective (lines 1890 and 2296).
- The check runs once per objective and is cached, so it is cheap. Null and empty dictionaries are guarded, and dead models and reserves are handled by the threat helper.
- Adds a clear [R1_HOME_CAPTURE] log line and removes no log lines.
- Applies cleanly on 5e70bc2 and on V9R (with offsets).
- The test turns the fix on and erases the override afterwards. It drives _evaluate_all_objectives and _assign_units_to_objectives, and fails on base for the right reason (base sends the unit home). The main case uses Smoke and Mirrors, so it also exercises the decoy flag. Guardrail tests cover a paying card, an enemy in reach, round 2, a keeper and param 0.
- The report is honest: it addresses one finding, says which ones it does not, and notes that Alpha and Beta also change. Its guardrail claims match the code: the cards at s7404 P1 (Secure Asset), s7422 P1 (Death Trap), s7451 P2 (Search and Scour) and s7468 P2 (Surveil the Foe) all count home, so the fix does not fire there.
reviews.summary:
On the code lens the design is ok. I found no real bug that changes play. The gate restores the base exactly, the patch merges onto V9R, and the test checks the fix and fails on base for the right reason. One cosmetic but real bug: every redirected unit gets the false OBJ-EXPLAIN-1 note 'home already has enough OC' in its decision record. Other gaps are minor: secondary cards (Burden of Trust) are ignored, pass 3 can still send units home, and HOLD_OBJECTIVE earmarks are not respected.

Two points matter for the decision:

1. **It cannot show a gain in the bench.** In all 3 fixtures every home starts held and the keeper stays (FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE is off), so the trigger never fires. Expect identical pairs.
2. **Its own plan was never measured.** At s7468 it sends no unit home, but the +6.86 alternative kept Alpha going home. It would also fire at s7403 r1 P2, where the base sends a unit home and the clearly better alternative (+8.67) also had a unit on home.

Before choosing it, run rollouts of the fix's full plan at s7468 and s7403. Do not pick it on bench grounds.

I did not run Godot (read-only). The test pass counts are the designer's claims; I checked the logic by reading the code and the save files.

issues.situation: Part (b) copies the action of the unit's capture candidate. For a support objective in the reach band (gap between M and M+2"), that action comes from _should_unit_advance (5e70bc2 ~11520). That function has no enemy or charge check. It also returns true for any unit whose ability TEXT contains 'advance' and 'charge'. The long-trip gate _should_unit_advance_long_trip (~11629) skips its M+12" charge check for the same text match. Every Ork unit in the bench roster has the Waaagh! text '...gains the Advance & Charge ability', and every Blade Champion has 'Martial Inspiration ... Advance & Charge'. The engine only allows a charge after an Advance when flags.effect_advance_and_charge is set (ChargePhase ~2019-2041). Support units are assigned in pass 3, after the pass-2.5 chase gate. In base, a support 'move' takes the normal-move path: T7-23 blends the move toward the charge target, and MOV-1/T7-14 keep shooting. With (b), the unit goes straight to BEGIN_ADVANCE and cannot charge, or shoot with non-[ASSAULT] guns (Stompa, Deffkoptas, pistols). Observed in both V9-era Custodes-mirror bench records (FIRETEST s96021, FT2 s96031). In round 2, P2 Blade Champion Beta was a support unit 10.4" / 11.3" from its objective. In base it made a normal move 'toward charge target Custodian Guard Gamma' and declared a charge. With (b) it would Advance and could not charge. In the Orks mirror and Custodes-vs-Orks fixtures, every Ork support unit in its reach band Advances in rounds 2-4. The waaagh_advance_charge cluster measured this pattern (an Ork unit Advances when a Normal move reaches charge range) at +6.14 and +10.03 VP in favour of the Normal move. The report's claim that (b) 'inherits RACE-1's gate (no enemy within M+12")' is false for the reach band, and the gate is bypassed for these units.
issues.proposed_change: Do not use the candidate's action string. Store RACE-1's long_adv bool on each candidate (candidates.append in _assign_units_to_objectives) and pass it in place of rh_actions. (b) switches to 'advance' only when all of these hold: (1) long_adv is true (never the (M, M+2] reach band); (2) _get_charge_intent(unit_id) is empty; (3) no enemy centroid is within M+12", unless the unit's engine flag flags.effect_advance_and_charge is true (never AIAbilityAnalyzerData text matching); (4) every ranged weapon is [ASSAULT], or no enemy is within M + max ranged range. Restricting (b) to battle_round == 1, where all the evidence lies, is a simpler safe option, but keep (2)-(4).

issues.situation: (b) also conflicts with a measured position: support units that only JOIN an objective the plan already covers. In V9's KEEPER-RELEASE (s7437 r1, Custodes vs Orks), a unit joining an objective that another unit reaches no later measured +8.0 VP with a Normal move and +1.0 with an Advance. That is why V9 walks such joiners. (b) Advances every 'reinforcing X (k units already committed)' support move. The supporting finding s7451 (+5.86) is a contested race (contest_race -13.7). The neutral Custodes-vs-Orks support-to-centre Advance was +2.42 (n=12). Most round-1 bench fires are joiners of stacks no enemy is racing for. Example: FT2 r1 P1 sends Blade Champions Beta/Gamma and Custodian Guard Alpha/Beta/Delta to obj_nml_2 as 'reinforcing (1-5 units already committed)'.
issues.proposed_change: In (b), Advance only when arriving sooner matters: the candidate has race_enemy_oc > 0 (a contest race is on), or no unit the plan already sends there arrives by the same turn. Otherwise keep the Normal move, the same rule as the keeper-release joiner.

issues.situation: Part (a) cannot fire in round 1 in any bench fixture. At deployment both home objectives are already held: Custodian Guard F's base overlaps area-large-14/-13 in both Custodes setups, and Ork Deffkoptas A/B, Warbikers D and Gutsmek overlap theirs. So friendly_oc > 0 and home_undefended_bonus = 0, and the bench measures (b) alone. The bench's own round-1 'second unit sent home' pattern is not touched: in FT2 r1 P1, Custodian Guard Gamma and Epsilon 'reinforce obj_home_1' already held by Guard Zeta. (a) only acts on empty homes. Later in the game (a) is consistent with the need ledger and looks harmless.
issues.proposed_change: No code change is needed for safety. State in the report that the bench result belongs to (b). If the cluster's bench symptom is to be addressed, a separate rule is needed for support units sent to a held_safe home with no projected threat.

issues.situation: The fire rate is understated. The report says about 1-3 per game. In the two V9-era Custodes-mirror bench records, (b) would turn 36 of 48 support moves into Advances: 18 in round 1 (4-5 units per side) and 18 in rounds 2-5. In 80 V5-era mirror records it is 905 of 1364 support moves (8.1 per game in round 1, 2.6 in round 2). Most of a Custodes army's round-1 forward moves become Advances, so this is the main behaviour change in the bench, backed by two positions. Side effect: the AI re-rolls any Advance roll of 1, and a 2 when it has 3+ CP. Command Re-roll is once per phase, and units move front to back, so an early support Advance can use the re-roll before the capturer's Advance.
issues.proposed_change: With the gating from the first two issues, the round-1 count drops to the contested long trips. Re-state the expected fire rate per fixture. Optionally do not spend Command Re-roll on a support-pass Advance.

reviews.fires_in_bench: Often, in every fixture, almost all from (b). Custodes mirror: I re-scored the support-pass decision cards of the two V9-era bench games (firetest_season, firetest_season2). The support unit's candidate for the chosen objective would be 'advance' in 36 of 48 support moves, about 18 per game: about 9 in round 1 (4-5 per side) and the rest in rounds 2-5. In 80 V5-era mirror records the rate is 11.3 per game. A charge the base unit declared that round is cancelled about 1 per game in the V9 records (P2 Blade Champion Beta in round 2, both games) and 0.08 per game in V5 records. Custodes vs Orks: the Custodes side is like the mirror, about 4-5 in round 1 plus later rounds. On the Ork side, every reach-band support move Advances in any round because every Ork unit text-matches Advance & Charge, so I estimate several per game. Orks mirror: no records; by reasoning, several per game on both sides, with rounds 2-4 cases costing charges and non-[ASSAULT] shooting. Part (a) fires 0 times in round 1 in all three fixtures, because both home objectives start held (verified against the hosting-area polygons), and rarely later. No identical pairs are expected.
reviews.strengths: It finds two real valuation mismatches in the support pass. (a) The WEIGHT_HOME_UNDEFENDED bonus (+9 x tempo) is paid again after this phase's commitments cover the home's OC need. (b) The support pass ignores the pace its own score was costed at. Both are behind one parameter, and FIX_R1_HOME_CAPTURE = 0 reproduces base exactly; the test checks this. It does not depend on FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE. (a) is narrowly gated: empty homes whose need is already covered. It cannot touch keepers or held homes, so the harmful guardrails (s7468 P2 Kommandos, s7451 P2 home hold) and s7404 are unchanged. (b) reproduces the measured s7451 r1 P2 alternative exactly (+5.86, n=36). In the measured positions, a Normal move to the same objective is never clearly better than an Advance, so the round-1 direction is supported. The report is honest that the cluster's main finding (s7468 Gamma) is not fixed. The design fires in all bench fixtures, so the benchmark can measure it.
reviews.summary: This design changes the bench almost entirely through part (b), not (a). (a) is sound, but it is inert in round 1 of all three fixtures because both home objectives start held. (b) makes most support moves Advances: about 18 per Custodes-mirror game in V9-era records, against the report's 1-3. Round-1 long trips with Assault-armed Custodian Guard are cheap and match s7451 (+5.86). The problem is that (b) copies a candidate action that the reach-band predicate and the RACE-1 gate compute without any real charge check. They text-match 'Advance & Charge' on every Ork unit (Waaagh!) and every Blade Champion (Martial Inspiration), but the engine refuses those charges. So in rounds 2-4, support-pass Orks and Blade Champions Advance where the base Normal move set up a charge or non-Assault shooting. That happened once per game in both V9 bench records, and the waaagh_advance_charge cluster measured this Ork pattern at +6 to +10 VP in favour of the Normal move. Advancing joiners also conflicts with the s7437 keeper measurement (walk +8.0 vs Advance +1.0). Revise: limit (b) to RACE-1 long trips with no charge intent and no enemy within M+12\" (engine flag only), only Assault guns or no targets after a Normal move, and preferably round 1 or contested races. Then benchmark.

issues.situation: (b) can make melee-capable support units give up a charge (rounds 2+, and round 1 for the second player in the Ork fixtures). Example: a support-pass Blade Champion, an Ork Mek, or Ork Warbikers whose 18" guns are out of range of an enemy 19-24" away, with the support objective a long trip. _should_unit_advance_long_trip skips its 'no enemy within M+12"' check for these units. The reason is that AIAbilityAnalyzer.unit_has_ability_containing reads the once-per-battle 'Waaagh!' / 'Martial Inspiration' text ('...gains the advance & charge ability') as Advance-and-charge. Every Ork unit and every Blade Champion in the bench rosters has this text. So the capture candidate is 'advance', and with (b) the support assignment becomes BEGIN_ADVANCE. The executor's Advance branch (base AIDecisionMaker.gd ~7043) skips the T7-23 charge-intent blending, and the unit cannot charge this turn. In the base, the support 'move' blends 70% toward a planned charge target and the unit can still charge. Support units are assigned after pass 2.5, so the melee chase gate never turns them into attacks. The report's risk note says (b) 'inherits RACE-1's gate (no enemy within M+12" unless Advance-and-charge)'. For these units that protection does not work.
issues.proposed_change: In the support pass, keep the candidate's 'advance' only when _get_charge_intent(unit_id) is empty and no enemy centroid is within the unit's M + 12". The only exception is a unit with the active flags.effect_advance_and_charge flag; do not trust the ability-text match. Optionally also limit (b) to battle_round == 1, where all of its evidence is (s7451 r1 P2 +5.86 clear; s7470 r1 P1 +2.42 neutral). Add a unit test: a support unit with that ability text, an enemy 14" away and a long trip to its support objective must keep action 'move'.

issues.situation: (a) cannot fire in the bench in round 1, and its own evidence is weak. All three fixtures start with both homes held. In the Custodes layouts Custodian Guard F has 5 models on the obj_home_1/obj_home_2 hosting areas (area-large-14/13). In the Ork layouts Deffkoptas A/B, Warbikers D and Wazdakka are on the homes. So friendly_oc > 0 and home_undefended_bonus = 0. Later rounds need a home that is already empty when the Movement phase starts, re-taken by a capture-pass unit, while a support unit prefers it. Two measured positions match (a)'s exact pattern (support 'reinforcing obj_home_1'), and neither supports it: s7411 r1 P1 movement_1_0, forward Move obj_nml_1, E -3.08 [-6.27, 0.10]; s7405 r1 P1 movement_1_0, E +0.25. The report covers neither. The cluster's main finding (s7468 Gamma, +6.86) is not changed; the report says so. In s7468, (a) only moves Alpha sideways from home to obj_nml_1, which other units already cover. The value of that change is not measured.
issues.proposed_change: State in the report that the bench result will measure (b) only. Do not count s7468 as addressed. Either keep (a) as unmeasured clean-up or split it into its own parameter, so a bench result for (b) is not credited to (a).

issues.situation: The report's firing rate ('1.8 per game', '1-3 per game') comes from replays of mid-phase finding positions, not from the bench fixtures. At P1's first Movement phase in each fixture, every P1 unit is at least 28.8" from the nearest enemy. So the long-trip gate passes for every P1 unit except the Stompa (100" guns). For the M5/M6 Custodes, trips to obj_center and the no-man's-land objectives (15-24") all have 'Advance saves a turn' (P >= 0.3), and so do many Ork trips. With one home keeper and about 3-4 capture-pass units, most remaining units go to the support pass and will now Advance. (b) is a much broader round-1 change than the report says.
issues.proposed_change: Count [R1_HOME_CAPTURE] log lines over rounds 1-2 of each bench fixture, both seat orders, with the fix on, and report that rate.

issues.situation: The decision checks ran on 5e70bc2 with FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE=1. In s7451 r1 P2, the '1 unit already committed' to obj_center appears to be Beta, the obj_home_2 keeper that KEEPER_RELEASE sent there. The movement_2_1 record shows the chosen option 'Hold obj_home_2' but the action 'Beta moves toward obj_center (capturing it (uncontrolled))'. The merge target V9R has the release OFF, so Beta keeps home. That changes support_counts, and possibly whether Gamma is a support unit at all. So the headline match has not been shown on the merge target.
issues.proposed_change: Re-run the unit test, the s7451/s7468 decision checks and the guardrails with FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE=0.

issues.situation: A battle-shocked holder can make the need ledger look covered. _unit_alive_oc does not zero a battle-shocked unit (MissionManager.model_oc does not apply battle-shock). Suppose a battle-shocked unit stands on an otherwise empty home: friendly_oc is 0 and the bonus is present. Pass 1 assigns it HOLD and sets obj_oc_remaining[home] to 0. (a) then removes the home bonus from every support unit, although the home has OC 0. In the base, the bonus still pulls a support unit there.
issues.proposed_change: Skip the (a) drop when the OC covering that objective comes from a battle-shocked holder. Alternatively, count a battle-shocked holder's OC as 0 in pass 1.

issues.situation: cand_actions also passes on 'advance' from the short-trip branch (gap between M and M+2, decided by _should_unit_advance). In round 1 that function returns true for any no-man's-land objective, even when the unit has shooting targets in range. So a support unit sent to an NML objective that is already covered gives up its non-Assault shooting only to reinforce it. That trade made sense for a capture, not for support.
issues.proposed_change: Take (b)'s Advance only from the RACE-1 long-trip branch (store a long_adv flag on the candidate and check it), or also require no enemy within weapon range.

issues.situation: Test gaps. The test drives the planner and fails on base for the right two reasons. But it has no negative case for (b): a support unit with an enemy in weapon range or charge reach should keep walking. It also never checks that a support 'advance' reaches the executor as BEGIN_ADVANCE.
issues.proposed_change: Add a negative (b) case: a ranged support unit with an enemy within 24" must keep 'move'. Add a decide-level assertion that the support unit's action is BEGIN_ADVANCE.

reviews.fires_in_bench: (a): about 0. In all three fixtures both homes start held at deployment. In the Custodes layouts Custodian Guard F has 5 models on the obj_home_1/2 hosting areas; in the Ork layouts Deffkoptas, Warbikers D and Wazdakka are on the homes. So neither home is empty in round 1 and the undefended bonus is 0. Later it needs a home that is already empty when a Movement phase starts, re-taken by a capture-pass unit, while a support unit prefers it: probably well under once per game. (b): fires in almost every game, mostly in round 1 for the player who goes first. At P1's first movement every P1 unit is at least 28.8" from the nearest enemy (Custodes mirror 28.8-36", asym 29.5-37", Orks mirror 29-49"). So _should_unit_advance_long_trip passes for every P1 unit except the Stompa. For the M5/M6 Custodes, trips to the centre and NML objectives (15-24") are 'Advance saves a turn', and so are many Ork trips. Each army has one home keeper and about 3-4 capture-pass units. That leaves about 5-7 Custodes units for the support pass (Prosecutors may be taken for screening at Hard), plus several Ork units; most choose centre or NML targets. Estimate: about 3-6 support Advances for P1 in round 1. For P2 in round 1, about 0-2: P1 is now inside 24" of the Custodes spears, but Blade Champions, the Mek and the 12-18" Ork guns still pass. A few more in rounds 2+. In total about 4-10 per game, well above the report's 1-3. The bench pairs will not be identical, but they will measure (b), not the home-capture correction.
reviews.strengths: Small, clean, fully gated patch. FIX_R1_HOME_CAPTURE=0 gives the base behaviour exactly: priority is unchanged, both new arguments are empty, and no new log lines print. The bonus share is tracked exactly, including tempo, and subtracted only once. Ids, empty dictionaries and types are handled correctly; `_dn` has a default argument. The extra loop runs once per support unit over the candidates, so the cost is trivial. No debug log is removed. The new logs print only when a correction changes the outcome. The root-cause trace for the second home unit is correct: the need ledger counts the first capturer, and the support pass paid WEIGHT_HOME_UNDEFENDED again. (b) reproduces exactly the measured alternative at s7451 r1 P2 (Gamma Advance obj_center, +5.86 clear, n=36); I confirmed Gamma is 36" from any enemy there, so its candidate is a long-trip Advance. s7470 r1 P1 (+2.42, neutral) also leans the same way. Hold, capture and keeper passes are untouched, so the guardrails (Kommandos and keepers holding home, capture-pass races) cannot change. The report is honest that the main s7468 finding is not fixed and why (contest_race, and the Smoke and Mirrors decoy scoring that the model does not credit). The test pins the fix on, erases the override, fails on base for the right two reasons, and drives the real planner from _evaluate_all_objectives through every pass.
reviews.summary: Patch: /home/user/warhammer-40k-godot/tools/ai_lab/r4_designs/r1_home_capture/root.patch. Report: /home/user/warhammer-40k-godot/tools/ai_lab/r4_designs/r1_home_capture/root.json. The patch applies cleanly to 5e70bc2 and parameter 0 gives the base behaviour exactly. The design has two parts. (a) stops paying the +9 home-undefended bonus to support units once the home's OC need is already covered. The idea is sound and the code is correct. But (a) cannot fire in the bench in round 1, because all three fixtures start with both homes held. Its two measured matching positions are neutral or negative (s7411 -3.08, s7405 +0.25), and it does not touch the cluster's main finding (s7468 Gamma). (b) lets a support-pass unit keep the Advance its capture candidate chose. This is the effective change: it matches the clear s7451 result and fires a lot in the bench, since almost every P1 support unit in round 1 passes the gate. So the bench will measure (b). (b) has one real defect. It relies on RACE-1's long-trip gate, whose charge-reach check is skipped for every Ork unit and every Blade Champion because of the ability-text match. Support units never pass through the melee chase gate. So with (b), Blade Champions, the Mek and out-of-range Ork units Advance toward a support objective when they could have charged, and they skip T7-23 charge-intent blending. Revise: keep (b)'s Advance only when the unit has no charge intent and no enemy is within M+12" (unless the real effect_advance_and_charge flag is set), and optionally limit (b) to round 1. Also add a negative test, count firings on the bench fixtures, and re-validate with FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE=0 (V9R). Not handled, though the cluster hint raised it: Custodian Guard with Assault spears still will not long-trip Advance once any enemy is within 24".

issues.situation: Every bench game, round 1: the bench can only see part (b), and part (b) is far broader than its evidence. Part (a) (round 1, state 'uncontrolled' only) cannot fire in any of the 3 fixtures: both homes are held at deployment (Custodian Guard Zeta, OC 10, stands on area-large-14/13 in the Custodes and asym fixtures; Deffkoptas x2 + Warbikers + Wazdakka, OC 25, on each Ork home; V9 bench records: 'Custodian Guard Zeta holds obj_home_1 (sole holder)'). This is the same reason V9's keeper fix gave 124/124 identical pairs. Part (b) instead hits nearly every round-1 forward support walk. The six V9 Custodes-mirror bench games (/tmp/v9check/20261030_163105_CHK_M1_96021.record.json.gz, scratchpad firetest_season*/) have 5-7 P1 and 3-5 P2 'reinforcing' Normal moves in round 1; across 471 stored mirror games the average is 5.8 / 3.5. Their decision records list the units' other long trips as 'Advance ... (advancing to arrive a turn sooner)', so long-trip Advance is allowed at the fixture's 29in+ gaps. The 'plan unit gets there first' test is strict (assignments[a].turns_to_reach < sa_c.turns_to_reach), while KEEPER-RELEASE, the lesson the design cites, uses <=. So the usual same-turn capture unit never counts (both arrive in 2 turns at the Advance pace: CHK P1 Blade Champion Alpha -> nml_2, Guard Gamma -> centre). In CHK, BC Beta, BC Gamma, Guard Alpha, Guard Beta and Guard Epsilon (P1) and 3/3 P2 walks all flip to Advance: about 5 (P1 seat) / 3 (P2 seat) changed decisions per game, vs the report's '0-2 per game per army'. Of these, 1.8-1.9 per side are lone Blade Champions, the fragile class part (a) exempts; their long-trip Advance permission comes only from the 'Martial Inspiration' text (once per battle in the profile, read as always-on by the AI's text check). Another 0.3-0.7 per game are support trips to the enemy home, which are lost races and so Advance regardless. Example harm for the P2 seat (geometry estimate, not measured): a lone BC Advancing toward a centre P1 already reached ends about 2in closer (8in Advance destination vs 6in walk) to P1's capture Guard, which moves first in round 2. P1's charge odds rise from roughly 40% to roughly 70%, and a 5x5 A S7 AP-2 D2 Guard charge deals about 14 damage to the 6-W BC. The bench verdict will therefore rest on a broad rule backed by one position (s7451 +5.86) and can neither credit nor blame part (a) (s7468 +6.86).
issues.proposed_change: (1) Put part (b) under its own switch and log tag (e.g. FIX_R1_SUPPORT_ADVANCE under the FIX_R1_HOME_CAPTURE master, tag '[R1_SUPPORT_ADVANCE]', logging only changed decisions) so the bench runs a (b)-off arm. (2) Narrow (b) to the s7451 shape. Count a plan unit that arrives the same turn as first (<=, as KEEPER-RELEASE does), so (b) fires only when the race is lost or every capture unit is strictly slower. Skip _lone_trip_fragile units (part (a) already does). Skip support trips to the enemy home and to an objective RACE-SKIP/TOO-LATE refused for this unit in pass 2 (extra_obj_skipped[unit].objective_id == sa_oid). In CHK this leaves about 1 flip per seat (P1 Guard Epsilon -> nml_1, P2 Guard Epsilon -> centre, both lost races). (3) Correct the fire estimate and run the bench with AI_LAB_KEEP_LOG_GREP containing the tags, so part (a)'s 0 fires and part (b)'s count are recorded. Give part (a) its own full-game (horizon 0) evidence at s7468-type positions, since the bench cannot see it.

issues.situation: Part (a) spare selection ignores arrival time. The spare is the first unassigned unit in score order with a move/advance home candidate, which may need 2 turns or a lucky Advance. At s7468 Alpha, 12.7in away, Advances home (gap ~8.9in, needs D6>=3, ~67%), while the deferred Gamma reached home with a Normal move (9.4in). When the primary pays for home at the next Command phase, the failed-roll games lose that VP, and the forward-VP comparison does not price it.
issues.proposed_change: Defer only when a non-deferred spare's home candidate arrives this turn at Normal pace (_capture_arrival(c).phases == 1), or when home's vp_value is 0. Otherwise capture as before.

issues.situation: The s7468 decision check claims an exact match, but the fix's plan is not the measured branch B. B forced only Gamma (Gamma Advances to the centre, Beta still Advances to obj_center, Alpha goes home). The fix also turns Beta into a Normal-move support trip to obj_nml_1, so one Guard unit fewer reaches the centre. The +6.86 does not cover the fix's plan.
issues.proposed_change: Re-measure the fix's own plan at s7468 (36 seeds), or have the check keep Beta's base order.

issues.situation: Ork seats (asym P2, Orks mirror). Part (b) inherits _should_unit_advance_long_trip's advance-and-charge bypass from the 'Waaagh!' ability text. The engine grants advance-and-charge only while Waaagh! is active; the confirmed findings s7468 r3 +6.14 and s7473 r3 +10.03 showed such Advances were wrong. In round 1, P2 Ork support units with short or no guns (Stormboyz, Mek, Wartrike, Gretchin: 0-12in, so the weapon-range gate rarely blocks them) Advance and lose real charges against P1 Kult of Speed units that Advanced to within about 15-20in.
issues.proposed_change: In part (b), require no enemy within M+12in of the unit at the start of the move unless flags.effect_advance_and_charge is set (the engine predicate), independent of ability text.

issues.situation: Leaks and merge conflicts. OBJ-ASSIGN-1's 'closer unit' search does not skip home_deferred units, so a deferred durable unit that is still unassigned can be chosen as the quicker taker of home and sent there anyway. Part (a) then fires less than intended. The post-pass-2 hunk's context is the KEEPER-RELEASE block, which V9R's keeper revision deletes and re-adds after pass 3, so the patch will not apply cleanly on V9R. V10's RI-ASSAULT also widens long-trip Advance permission for all-[ASSAULT] units (Custodian Guard) when enemies are in weapon range, which will raise part (b)'s fire rate further.
issues.proposed_change: Skip home_deferred units in the OBJ-ASSIGN-1 alt loop for a home_last objective. Rebase on V9R, keeping part (a)'s post-pass right after pass 2 and before pass 2.5. Re-count part (b) fires on V10 with RI-ASSAULT on.

reviews.fires_in_bench: Part (a): 0 in all three fixtures. It acts only in round 1 on an uncontrolled home, and both homes are held at deployment: Custodian Guard Zeta (OC 10) on each Custodes home area; Deffkoptas x2, Warbikers and Wazdakka (OC 25) on each Ork home. V9 bench records show 'Custodian Guard Zeta holds obj_home_1 (sole holder)', the same situation that made round 3's keeper fix give 124/124 identical pairs. Part (b): fires in every Custodes-mirror game. V9 bench records have 5-7 P1 and 3-5 P2 round-1 'reinforcing' Normal moves (471 stored mirror games: 5.8 / 3.5 per game), whose candidates are 2-turn long-trip Advances. The strict '<' first-arrival test lets almost all of them flip: about 5 changed decisions when the candidate is P1 and about 3 when P2, about 4 per game, so no identical pairs are expected. Asym: about 5 for the Custodes P1 seat (same deployment). The Ork P2 seat was not measured but likely has several (every unit except the Stompa may Advance long trips at P1's start, and the Waaagh! text bypasses the charge-range guard). Orks mirror: not measured, likely several per seat. The bench therefore measures part (b) only.
reviews.strengths: Part (a) is well guarded and reuses existing helpers. It applies only in round 1, to an uncontrolled home with nothing heading there. _keeper_release_threat covers the enemy's next turn: on-board reach M+18in to the hosting area, plus reserves from round 2 and early-arrival rules. Card checks are correct: hold_home_required, Defend Stronghold and Extend Battle Lines block it, and Burden of Trust correctly does not. Fragile and HOLD_OBJECTIVE-earmarked units are exempt, holders and keepers are untouched, and it does not depend on FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE. Home is never left open while a unit can take it: a spare takes it, or else the deferred unit whose forward trip is worth least returns and its forward OC need re-opens. It reproduces the s7468 flip and leaves all guardrails unchanged. Its direction (durable units forward) matches the round-2 lesson that units held back scored less. Part (b)'s Advance direction agrees with several measured round-1 positions besides s7451 (+5.86): walking instead of Advancing was harmful for Lootas B (-6.67), Scout Squad B (-5.00) and s7470 Lootas (-5.50). The design is param-gated, logs every change with a tag, and its tests fail on base and pass with the fix.
reviews.summary: The idea is sound, but the bench will not measure it as designed. Part (a), which carries the cluster's main finding (s7468 +6.86), cannot fire in any bench fixture because both homes are held at deployment. Part (b) turns nearly every round-1 forward support walk into an Advance: about 5 per P1 seat and 3 per P2 seat in each Custodes-mirror game. That includes lone Blade Champions, whose Advance permission comes only from the misread 'Martial Inspiration' text, and enemy-home trips, all on the strength of one position (s7451). It fires this widely because its 'gets there first' test is strict (<), unlike KEEPER-RELEASE's <=. Revise: split (b) under its own switch and tag; narrow it to lost-race trips with a <= first-arrival test; skip fragile, enemy-home and RACE-SKIP'd units; check that the spare taking home arrives this turn; rebase on V9R; and give part (a) full-game evidence outside the bench.

issues.situation: Part (a), the home deferral behind the s7468 +6.86 finding, cannot fire in any of the 3 bench fixtures. Every home objective is already held at deployment by a unit overlapping its 11e hosting ruin (the 7"x11.5" rectangles area-large-14/13). Custodes lists: Custodian Guard F centroid (645,661) is inside the obj_home_1 polygon (x 560-840, y 240-700), with its nearest model 3.78" from the marker. Orks mirror: Deffkoptas A/B, Warbikers D and Wazdakka sit on each home. Asym P2: Deffkoptas A/B, Warbikers A/B and Wazdakka sit on obj_home_2. The plan is built once per movement phase (COORD-4 persistent plan) while the keeper holds. FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE is off in V9R, and AGGRO-FREE needs 10+ models, so `state == "uncontrolled"` is never true in round 1. Only part (b) can produce bench differences. The report's 'fires' section counts finding replays only and never addresses the fixtures.
issues.proposed_change: Give part (b) its own param (e.g. FIX_R1_SUPPORT_ADVANCE) so the bench can attribute effects. State in the report that the home deferral is dormant in all three fixtures, so the bench cannot confirm the +6.86. If part (a) needs full-game evidence, use a fixture or seed set where home starts empty.

issues.situation: Part (b) treats 'a unit of the plan gets there first' as strictly sooner (`turns_to_reach < sa_c.turns_to_reach`), so a tie counts as nobody being first and the unit Advances. The report cites the keeper_release lesson, but that code's kr_first uses `<=`: a unit arriving no later means a Normal move. At the bench deployments every first-player unit is 29-36" (Custodes) or 29-49" (Orks) from the nearest enemy, so RACE-1's _should_unit_advance_long_trip passes for all of them. Nearly every centre or NML trip is then a 2-Advance-turn candidate, and the pass-2 capturer of that objective also arrives in 2 turns. Result: almost every leftover support unit of the first player Advances, even in uncontested races. That is far broader than the report's '0-2 per game per army' and goes beyond the one measured position (s7451, a lost race).
issues.proposed_change: Use `<=` for the other assignment's turns_to_reach, matching keeper_release's kr_first. Keep the Advance whenever sa_c.race_lost is true; s7451 still Advances because its race is lost. Add a unit test where the support unit ties with an uncontested capturer and must make a Normal move.

issues.situation: OBJ-ASSIGN-1 can hand home straight back to a deferred unit during pass 2. When a non-deferred (fragile or earmarked) unit's home candidate is processed, the 'closer unit' search scans unassigned units' home candidates. A deferred durable unit is still unassigned there, because its forward candidates come later in score order. Its home score is higher, so it passes the 4.0 margin; if it is also at least 3" quicker, it takes home ('quicker to reach than ...'). The deferral is silently undone and the plan falls back to base. Example: the design's own fragile-squad test with alpha placed closer to home than the squad.
issues.proposed_change: In the OBJ-ASSIGN-1 alt loop add `if home_last.has(oid) and home_deferred.has(alt.unit_id): continue`.

issues.situation: The VP guard only checks that SOME forward capture worth at least home's vp_value exists (home_last_forward returns the first such candidate). After deferral the unit simply takes its next pass-2 candidate. That can be a higher-scored forward objective worth LESS VP than home, which the stated rule ('a forward capture worth at least the home VP that pass 2 would send it on') excludes. Separately, the support pass still prices the deferred home with +9 WEIGHT_HOME_UNDEFENDED, so a leftover unit can still be stacked onto home as support (the cluster's 'second unit' pattern). That pattern is only avoided where geometry happens to prevent it, as at s7468.
issues.proposed_change: Store hl_fwd per deferred unit. While that unit is unassigned in pass 2, skip its non-home candidates whose vp_value is below home_vp, or assign hl_fwd directly when it is still open. Optionally exclude home_last objectives from _find_best_remaining_objective for round-1 support, since a spare already takes them.

issues.situation: The spare and pull-back selection (post-pass-2 block) does not require reaching home this turn. It also bypasses TOO-LATE and RACE-SKIP, because the deferral `continue` runs before those checks. The first spare loop can only ever find units whose home trip those checks skipped. If the chosen unit needs 2 turns, home is not held at our next Command phase and that round's home VP is lost. Meanwhile the deferred unit's forward trip is often 2 turns too, so the vp_value comparison weighs a next-round score against a later one.
issues.proposed_change: Choose the spare or pull-back only among units whose home candidate arrives this turn (`_capture_arrival(c).phases == 1`, or an Advance candidate). If none qualifies, do not defer (keep the base assignment). Apply too_late and race_hopeless in both spare loops.

issues.situation: Part (b)'s turn filter is inconsistent. `turns_to_reach < 2 -> break` drops RACE-1 long-trip candidates that reach in 1 turn at the Advance pace (gap in (M+2, ~M+3.5]), where Advancing has at least a 30% chance to arrive now. Short-path Advance candidates (gap <= M+2) pass, because their turns_to_reach is stored at the Normal pace (2). Those come from _should_unit_advance, whose round-1 NML rule returns true even with shooting targets in range, and nothing checks for an enemy within charge reach. The report describes the trigger as RACE-1 only.
issues.proposed_change: Compute Normal-pace turns explicitly (ceil(gap/M)) and Advance when the Advance-pace turns are lower. Alternatively, restrict part (b) to RACE-1 long-trip candidates (store a long_adv flag on the candidate) and document this.

issues.situation: The patch does not apply to V9R, the merge target (`git apply --check` fails at line 10373). Hunk 4's trailing context is the KEEPER-RELEASE block, which the keeper revision moves after pass 3. `patch --fuzz=3` 'succeeds' but puts the R1 post-block after pass 3 (V9R line ~10928), which silently changes behaviour. It then puts hunk 5 inside _decide_engaged_unit, inside a dictionary literal (parse error).
issues.proposed_change: Hand-merge: put the R1 post-block right after pass 2's final `apply_capture_assignment.call(cand)` (V9R ~10483, before '# PASS 2.5 (COORD-4)'). Put the support block right after the `_find_best_remaining_objective(...)` call (~10833). Re-run the test on V9R.

issues.situation: The s7468 decision check says the fix 'matches the alternative exactly'. In the measured branch B only Gamma's order was overridden. The persistent plan kept the base orders for Alpha (home, support) and Beta (Advance to obj_center). The fix also changes Beta to a Normal-move support of obj_nml_1. The fix's full plan is therefore not branch B, and the +6.86 covers only Gamma's part.
issues.proposed_change: Replay the fix's full round-1 plan (or also force Beta's new order) over paired seeds and report E for it. Otherwise state that only the decider's choice matches the measured alternative.

issues.situation: Test gaps. Part (b)'s 'no unit of the plan gets there first' branch is untested, and so is the guardrail 'joining a unit that arrives first stays a Normal move'; the only (b) test is a lost race whose lead arrives sooner. No test has a forward objective worth less VP than home, and the first spare loop is never exercised. Assertions read the plan dict rather than the executed BEGIN_ADVANCE. The executor does honour action 'advance' for any assign_pass, so this last gap is acceptable.
issues.proposed_change: Add three cases: (1) an uncontested objective where the capturer arrives the same turn as the support unit (expect a Normal move under `<=`); (2) an objective nobody else goes to (expect an Advance); (3) a card that pays more for home than for the forward objective (expect no deferral).

reviews.fires_in_bench:
These are estimates from the code's trigger conditions and the decoded fixture saves (/home/user/warhammer-40k-godot/40k/tests/saves/{mirror_custodes,asym,mirror_orks}_2000_postdeploy.w40ksave). I did not run the planner.

PART (a), the R1-HOME-LAST deferral: 0 fires in all 3 fixtures, for both seats. Each home objective is already held at deployment by a unit overlapping its 11e hosting ruin:
- Custodes: Custodian Guard F is inside obj_home_1 and obj_home_2.

reviews.strengths:

- Card handling is sensible: a primary that requires holding home, or a home hint, keeps base behaviour, while Burden of Trust ('any objective') does not block the deferral.
- Part (b) reuses RACE-1's own Advance decision, which already requires no lost shooting or charge, and the executor honours plan action 'advance' for support assignments.
- Clear [R1_HOME_CAPTURE] logs; the patch removes no lines; no new static state; negligible cost (one threat scan per plan, small candidate loops).

It drives the real planner (_evaluate_all_objectives plus _assign_units_to_objectives) and covers these guardrails: enemy near home, card pays, round 2, fragile unit, lone unit, param 0.
reviews.summary:
The code is sound. I found no crash, gating or null-access bug. Param 0 and rounds 2-5 restore the base exactly, and the test fails on base for the right reasons and drives the real planner. Verdict: ok, with minor issues.

The main concern is shipping relevance:
- **Part (a) never fires in the bench.** All three fixtures start with a unit standing on each home objective (inside its 11e hosting ruin), so the home deferral behind the s7468 +6.86 finding is dormant there.
- **Part (b) fires broadly.** The strict `<` in "gets there first" means almost every first-player leftover support unit Advances in round 1, even in uncontested races. The evidence for that is one measured position (s7451, a lost race).
- **Recommendation:** split part (b) into its own param and use `<=`, as keeper_release does, so it fires only for lost races or sole arrivals. That keeps s7451 and lets the bench attribute effects.

Smaller holes:
- OBJ-ASSIGN-1 can give home back to a deferred unit during pass 2.
- The VP guard does not constrain where the deferred unit actually goes.
- The spare unit is not required to reach home this turn.
- Part (b)'s turn filter is inconsistent between short and long Advance trips.
- The s7468 check overstates the match: in the measured branch Beta's plan was unchanged, but the fix also moves Beta.
- The patch needs a hand merge onto V9R: a fuzzy apply misplaces hunk 4 and puts hunk 5 inside _decide_engaged_unit.
